ruleset.name: Unused formal parameters
ruleset.description:
Second PHPMD leg: UnusedFormalParameter only.
This rule lives in its own ruleset because PHPMD honours <exclude-pattern> ONLY as a direct child of <ruleset>; nested inside a <rule> it is parsed and discarded (ConductionNL/.github#155). phpmd.xml carried exactly such a nested pattern (`*Migration*`) and it suppressed nothing: a baseline-neutralised run still reported 152 UnusedFormalParameter hits in lib/Migration.
A direct child, however, is applied by PDepend at file-collection time and drops the file from EVERY rule in the ruleset. Isolating UnusedFormalParameter here means the lib/Migration exclusion applies to this rule and this rule ALONE - every other rule still analyses lib/Migration in the main leg. That matters concretely: lib/Migration also holds 10 non-UnusedFormalParameter findings (3 ExcessiveMethodLength, 3 ElseExpression, 2 NPathComplexity, 2 CyclomaticComplexity). A top-level exclude in phpmd.xml would have swallowed all 10 silently.
Why lib/Migration is excluded from THIS rule: OCP\Migration\IMigrationStep mandates changeSchema(IOutput $output, Closure $schemaClosure, array $options) and preSchemaChange/postSchemaChange with the same three parameters. A step that needs none of them still cannot drop them. The signature cannot change.
NOTE the pattern is `*/lib/Migration/*`, not `*/Migration/*`. This repo also has lib/Service/Migration/LegacyToRegisterMigrator.php - an ordinary service, not an OCP migration step - which carries 1 genuine UnusedFormalParameter finding plus 11 other findings. The broader pattern would have excluded it from this rule for no reason.
